verses.text: When the uproar was over, Paul sent for the followers and encouraged them. Then he said goodbye and left for Macedonia.
He travelled through that area and encouraged the believers with many words. Then he came to Greece.
He stayed there three months. Some Jews made a plan against him as he was about to sail for Syria, so he decided to go back through Macedonia.
These men went with him as far as Asia: Sopater from Beroea, Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica, Gaius from Derbe, Timothy, and Tychicus and Trophimus from Asia.
These men went ahead and waited for us at Troas.
After the days of Unleavened Bread, we sailed from Philippi. Five days later we joined them at Troas, and we stayed there seven days.
On the first day of the week, we met together to break bread. Paul talked with the people. He planned to leave the next day, so he kept on talking until midnight.
There were many lamps in the upstairs room where we were meeting.
A young man named Eutychus was sitting in the window. He became very sleepy as Paul talked on and on. At last he fell fast asleep and fell from the third floor. When they picked him up, he was dead.
Paul went down, threw himself on the young man and put his arms around him. He said, "Do not be upset. He is alive!"
Then Paul went back upstairs, broke bread and ate. He talked with them for a long time, until the sun came up. Then he left.
The people took the young man home alive, and they were greatly comforted.
We went ahead to the ship and sailed for Assos. We planned to take Paul on board there. He had arranged this, because he wanted to go there on foot.
When he met us at Assos, we took him on board and went on to Mitylene.
The next day we sailed from there and arrived opposite Chios. The day after that we crossed over to Samos, and the next day we reached Miletus.
Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus so he would not spend time in Asia. He was in a hurry to reach Jerusalem, if he could, by the day of Pentecost.
From Miletus, Paul sent a message to Ephesus and asked the elders of the church to come to him.
When they arrived, he said to them, "You know how I lived among you the whole time, from the first day I came to Asia.
I served the Lord with all humility and with tears. I went through hard times because of the plans of the Jews against me.
You know I did not hold back anything that would help you. I taught you in public and from house to house.
I told both Jews and Greeks that they must turn away from sin, turn to God, and believe in our Lord Jesus.
And now the Spirit is pushing me to go to Jerusalem. I do not know what will happen to me there.
I only know that in every city the Holy Spirit warns me that prison and troubles are waiting for me.
But my life means nothing to me. I only want to finish my race with joy, and finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me. That work is to tell the good news of God's grace.
And now I know that none of you, among whom I went about preaching God's Kingdom, will ever see me again.
So I tell you today that I am not to blame if any of you are lost.
I did not hold back from telling you everything God wants.
Take care of yourselves and of all the flock. The Holy Spirit has made you leaders over it. Be shepherds of God's church, which he bought with his own blood.
I know that after I leave, fierce wolves will come in among you. They will not spare the flock.
Even some men from your own group will rise up and twist the truth. They will try to pull the followers away after them.
So watch out! Remember that for three years I never stopped warning each of you, night and day, with tears.
Now, brothers, I give you to God and to the message of his grace. That message can build you up and give you a share among all God's holy people.
I have never wanted anyone's silver, gold or clothes.
You know that I worked with my own hands to provide for myself and for the people who were with me.
In everything I showed you that by working hard like this, we must help the weak. Remember the words the Lord Jesus himself said: 'It is more blessed to give than to receive.'"
When Paul had finished speaking, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
They all cried a lot. They hugged Paul and kissed him.
What made them saddest was that he had said they would never see him again. Then they went with him to the ship.
